footnoteDefinitions.1: Agency provides services under a federal waiver program to a non-traditional, chronic long-term population.
footnoteDefinitions.2: Agency provides services to a special-needs population.
footnoteDefinitions.4: The number of patient episodes for this measure is too small to report.
footnoteDefinitions.5: No current data, or provider certified/recertified for less than six months.
footnoteDefinitions.6: National average not provided because of state-to-state data-collection differences.
footnoteDefinitions.7: Medicare is not displaying rates for any agency because of a data issue.
footnoteDefinitions.9: Zero or very few patients met survey inclusion rules; available scores may not accurately describe the agency.
footnoteDefinitions.10: Survey results are based on less than 12 months of data.
footnoteDefinitions.11: Fewer than 70 patients completed the survey; use available scores with caution.
footnoteDefinitions.12: No survey results are available for this period.
footnoteDefinitions.13: CMS suppressed data for one or more quarters.

interpretationRules: Results belong to the exact six-character CCN. A CCN may encompass multiple branches; it is not necessarily a single street office or an entire brand network.
Survey percentages, four domain star ratings, and the published summary star are distinct measures. Recommendation has no published star rating in this release.
All seven matched entities have numeric survey results and no populated survey footnote fields in this release. This does not remove nonresponse, sampling or time-lag limitations.
CMS survey stars require at least 40 completed surveys over four quarters; footnote 11 cautions on fewer than 70. These are different thresholds.
Retain missing raw values and footnotes; never convert blanks, NA, Not Available or a dash to zero stars or zero percent.
Use official state/national values for the same period only as descriptive context, not statistical proof that an agency is better.
Do not multiply adjusted percentages by completed-survey counts to invent a number of favorable respondents.
The survey was revised beginning April 2026. This public reporting period ends March 2026, so these are original-survey measures. Do not relabel them with future revised-survey questions.
